content.title: About
content.content: Chili is a hot pepper derived from various Capsicum cultivars. The NFS (New Fresh Spice) version is a fresh, non‑dried pepper that retains maximum aroma and heat. Chili is widely used in cooking to add spiciness and is a key ingredient in sauces, marinades, and spice blends.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Capsaicin, the compound responsible for heat, also has mild analgesic properties.
Different chili varieties are measured on the Scoville scale, ranging from mild sweet (0–500) to extreme (over 1,000,000).
Chili was used in traditional medicine by ancient Mesoamerican cultures to aid digestion.
Dried chili can be stored for up to a year, while fresh NFS should be used within 7‑10 days.
In some cultures chili is considered a protective talisman against evil spirits.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Capsaicin and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Capsaicin may increase calorie burning and help with weight management.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Antioxidant properties help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A is essential for vision and skin health.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Consuming large amounts of hot chili can cause heartburn or gastric irritation.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to capsaicin or other pepper components.

items.title: Increased body temperature
items.content: Capsaicin triggers sweating and a feeling of heat, which may be uncomfortable with fever.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Hot peppers can enhance the effects of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for users of such drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fresh NFS chili can be thinly sliced and added to salads, soups, sauces, and marinades. It is also used to make spicy pastes, chips, and flavored oils. To reduce heat, remove the seeds and inner membrane.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh chili in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 5‑7 days. For longer preservation, freeze it in bags or dry it; dried chili keeps well in a cool, dark place for up to a year.
